findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, such as `main; touch /tmp/pwned`, `exec` executes the appended command with the process's privileges. The previous `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` implementation passed the branch literally and avoided shell interpretation. Retain `execFile` or otherwise avoid invoking a shell.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the Git process
findings.body:
`exec()` returns the shell process rather than necessarily the `git` process. On Windows, or shells that retain a wrapper process, calling `.kill()` on the returned child during a long-running `git show` terminates only the shell; Git can continue consuming resources, and `close` may remain delayed while it holds inherited pipes. `execFile()` previously made Git the directly cancellable child.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element instead of invoking a shell
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command. Any caller passing attacker-controlled input such as `HEAD; <command>` allows arbitrary command execution with the process’s privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation treated the branch as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argv element instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so any untrusted branch value containing shell syntax executes arbitrary commands with the process’s privileges—for example, `showBranch("main; touch /tmp/pwned")`. The previous `execFile` implementation safely passed the value as one argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass branch names without invoking a shell
findings.body:
On POSIX, a valid branch string such as `main;sleep${IFS}60` executes `sleep 60`. Repeated untrusted inputs can retain child processes and descriptors until process-table exhaustion; other payloads can consume unbounded CPU. `execFile` previously passed the branch literally.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
